pride_data.title: MACSPI Enables Tissue-Selective Proteomic and Interactomic Analyses  in Multicellular Organisms
pride_data.projectDescription: Multicellular organisms are composed of many tissue types that have distinct morphologies and functions, which are largely driven by specialized proteomes and interactomes. To define the proteome and interactome of a specific type of tissue in an intact animal, we developed a localized proteomics approach called Methionine Analog-based Cell-Specific Proteomics and Interactomics (MACSPI). This method uses the tissue-specific expression of an engineered methionyl-tRNA synthetase (MetRS) to label proteins with a bifunctional amino acid photo-ANA in selected cells. We applied MACSPI in Caenorhabditis elegans, a model multicellular organism, to selectively label, capture, and profile the proteomes of the body wall muscle and the nervous system, which led to the identification of new tissue-specific proteins. Using the photo-crosslinker, we successfully profiled HSP90 interactors in muscles and neurons and identified tissue-specific interactors and stress-related interactors. Our study demonstrates that MACSPI can be used to profile tissue-specific proteomes and interactomes in intact multicellular organisms.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: We fed the transgenic C. elegans expressing the CeMetRS L43G mutant with bacteria grown in either ‘heavy’ medium containing photo-ANA or ‘light’ medium containing methionine. C. elegans were harvested and lysed as described above. The protein concentration was determined by BCA Protein Assay (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and diluted to 1 mg/mL. The 2 mg of lysates extracted from “heavy” and “light” were pooled together at 1:1 ratio and then reacted with 100 μM cleavable biotin-azide by “click” chemistry, followed with 1 mM TCEP, 100 M TBTA and 1 mM CuSO4, vortexed and incubated for 1.5 hours at room temperature. 4 volumes of Iice-cold acetone was added to precipitate proteins for at least 2 hours. The samples were spined and washed twice with 15 mL of ice-cold methanol. Protein pellets were dried in air for 10 min and dissolved in 1 mL of PBS with 20 mM EDTA, 4% SDS and 10% glycerol by vortex. Samples were then heated at 75 ℃ for 8 min and diluted with PBS to an SDS concentration of 0.5%. Pre-equilibrated high-capacity streptavidin agarose beads (Thermo Fisher Scientific) were added to protein samples and incubated at room temperature for 2 hours with rotating. The streptavidin beads were sequentially washed with 1 mL of PBS containing 0.2% SDS for 6 times, 1 mL of 6 M urea in PBS with 0.1% SDS for 6 times, and 1 mL of 250 mM NH4HCO3 with 0.05% SDS for 6 times. Enriched proteins were eluted by 100 L of 25 mM Na2S2O4 and 0.05% SDS in 250 mM NH4HCO3 for 1 hour with shaking at room temperature. The filtrate was collected and dried by SpeedVac. The dried proteins were resuspended with 30 L of 1 × LDS sample loading buffer containing 50 mM DTT, heated at 75 °C for 8 min, and then reacted with 130 mM iodoacetamide in the dark for 30 min to alkylate all the reduced cysteines. Enriched proteins were then separated by NuPAGETM 4-12% Bis-Tris gel, followed by fixation with a 50% methanol/7% acetic acid solution at room temperature for 15 min. The fixed gel was washed three times with ddH2O for 30 min, stained with Gelcode Blue Staining and finally washed three times with ddH2O for 30 min. Each lane of the gel was sliced into 8 pieces and further diced into 1 mm cubes by using the Mickle Gel Slicer and scalpel. The diced 1 mm cubes of gels were then destained by incubating with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate/50% acetonitrile for 1 hour. The destained gel cubes were dehydrated in acetonitrile for 10 min and digested in 25 mM NH4HCO3 containing 12.5 ng/mL trypsin at 37 ℃ for 12 hours. After digestion, the supernatant was collected and concentrated by SpeedVac to nearly dry, and then the samples were diluted with 0.1% trifluoroacetic up to 100 L. The resulting peptides were desalted and enriched with C18 StageTips. The StageTips were washed with 0.5% acetic acid three times and the resulting peptides were eluted with 100 L of 60% ACN and 0.5% acetic acid. The elutes were dried by SpeedVac and redissolved in LC-MS grade water with 0.1% formic acid for following LC-MS/MS analysis.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: For the estimation of the incorporation rate of “heavy” amino acid in E. coli, raw data were searched against the Uniprot E. coli database (UP000000625) with common contaminants using MaxQuant (1.6.10). Cysteine carbamidomethylation was set as a fixed modification, and methionine oxidation and protein amino-terminus acetylation were set as variable modifications. Mass error tolerance was set at 6 ppm for MS1 spectra and 20 ppm for MS2 spectra, and the maximum missed cleavages were set to 2. The false discovery rate (FDR) for peptide and protein was set to 0.01. For other proteomic experiments, Proteome Discoverer (v.2.5) was used to search raw data against the Uniprot C. elegans database (UP000001940). The following modifications were included: cysteine carbamidomethylation as a fix modification, methionine oxidation, protein N-terminus acetylation, and [13C615N4] arginine and [13C615N2] lysine as variable modifications. Mass error tolerance was set at 20 ppm for MS1 spectra and 0.05 Da for MS2 spectra, and maximum missed cleavages were set to 2. The FDR for peptide and protein was set to 0.01.
